title: What is the shortest path for a spider on a box?
description: Two faces of the box are laid flat side by side, so the spider's path becomes a straight line across a rectangle. The three ways of joining two faces are drawn and measured, and the shortest is picked. Keeko's doubt is that walking along the edges is shortest.
teaching_notes: One idea: lay two faces flat, and the shortest path is a straight line across them. Watch for students who add up the edge lengths and call that the shortest walk.

source: Shortest Path in a Box! There is a spider in a corner of a box. It wants to reach the farthest opposite corner. Since it cannot fly, it can reach the opposite point only by walking on the surfaces of the box. What is the shortest path it can take? Take a cardboard box and mark the path that you think is the shortest from one corner to its opposite corner.
video_script.why: The child can draw a rectangle and measure a line with a ruler, and now uses a flat drawing to find a shortest path on a box.
video_script.substitution: A box 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high, with the spider walking over two faces.
video_script.anchor: a box 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high with a spider at one corner
video_script.wrong_answer: walking along the edges is the shortest
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the three edges, 6 + 4 + 3 = 13, and calls the edge walk the shortest, but a straight line across two faces is shorter than that.
video_script.payoff_line: The shortest path is about nine point two centimetres

final_answer.value: About 9.2 cm, across the 6 by 4 face and the 6 by 3 face laid flat
final_answer.spoken: the shortest path is about nine point two centimetres, across the six by four face and the six by three face laid flat

maths_rules: on a flat sheet the shortest path between two spots is a straight line
lay two faces flat side by side; the spider's path becomes the diagonal of the joined rectangle
join along the 4 cm edge: 4 cm along and 6 + 3 = 9 cm across, diagonal about 9.8 cm
join along the 3 cm edge: 3 cm along and 6 + 4 = 10 cm across, diagonal about 10.4 cm
join along the 6 cm edge: 6 cm along and 4 + 3 = 7 cm across, diagonal about 9.2 cm
the shortest is about 9.2 cm; the edge walk is 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 cm, which is longer
video_script.design: The box stays in the anchor band with the spider at one corner. Two faces are unfolded flat in turn, the diagonal is drawn across each joined rectangle, and a ruler measures it.
